overview_markdown:
Ouroboros is an open-source, general-purpose AI agent whose defining trait is *self-modification*: it can rewrite the very implementation it runs on — code, architecture, prompts, tools, and dependencies — while preserving a continuous identity, durable memory, and history across tasks and restarts. It coordinates a live swarm of specialist sub-agents and works on external projects, positioning itself as an experiment in genuinely autonomous, self-evolving software.

Architecturally, it runs as a native desktop app (macOS, Windows, Debian/RPM Linux packages) or a headless CLI, keeping its repository, memory, and history on the local machine. Model inference is flexible: remote APIs you configure, or a fully local GGUF model for offline use. An accompanying OuroborosHub acts as a skills marketplace, and the project maintains unusually rigorous engineering hygiene — the commit log shows typed tool-argument refusals, trace-based self-check evidence, plan-review honesty gates, and a CONTRIBUTING.md that mandates a separate-agent review flow for any changes.

Compared to OpenClaw, Ouroboros trades ecosystem breadth and multi-channel messaging for a singular focus on persistent identity and self-improvement. It is arguably the more ambitious research artifact (with an arXiv technical report), but its self-rewriting nature makes it inherently higher-risk to run unsupervised, and its community and plugin ecosystem remain far smaller than OpenClaw's.
